title: Notes API, sign-in and webhooks: API and identity run
subject: 60 plan cases on mock services; 14 cases run against deliberately broken services
note: A failing mutant case is a defect found in a seeded broken service. A negative case that ends in a designed rejection counts as passed. Secrets and tokens are redacted at source.

run.tool: Typed API, identity and webhook steps

acceptance.text: Sign-in with an authorization code and PKCE gives verified tokens, and the notes API serves the signed-in tenant.
Sign-in rejects invalid ID tokens: expired, bad signature, wrong audience, forbidden algorithm, unpinned key, wrong nonce or state.
The notes API rejects expired, badly signed, wrong-audience and alg-none bearer tokens.
A tenant cannot list, read, create, update or delete another tenant's notes, and a read-only token cannot write.
Webhooks are verified: valid signatures accepted, forged, stale and duplicate deliveries handled.
LTI 1.3 launches are verified: tampered, replayed, unknown-deployment and mismatched-claim launches are rejected.
The client copes with rate limits and timeouts: it waits as told, gives up within limits and tells the user.
Writes are idempotent and batch calls report each item's outcome.
Addresses taken from server responses stay on the allow-list; private and off-list redirects are refused.
A failing assertion is reported with the expected and observed values (seeded failing check).

findings.title: Resilience outcome without a spec statement (timeout)
findings.caption: Request timed out; the spec does not say what the client does next
findings.reason: The plan ended in a resilience failure and the spec does not state the required behaviour.
findings.action: Decide whether the client should retry, give up or degrade, and add an acceptance criterion.
